narrative: 片头字幕、定格动画式的纸艺、一个从纸张材料中剪出来的身影：硬光或窗光，展现出纸张的边缘和撕裂处的纤维。拼贴（Collage）则是层层叠叠的碎片。
纸艺风让纸成为整个世界的材质。当纸被整齐地折成折面时，它是错误的工具；当人只是站在一间图书馆里时，也是错误的用法。
展现出剪切的痕迹和纤维。
how: 平视高度，35mm到50mm焦段，固定机位。以掠射角度照亮纸张纹理的光线。
撕裂的边缘、可见的纤维、剪影式的人物。Prompt: Paper world of [Subject], torn stock, visible fibers, a person as a cut-out on pulp.
when: 一张片头静帧、一个剪影式的身影、一个由纸浆构成的世界。不要把它当作折纸风来用，也不要用在一个人拿着一张纸当道具的场景上。
vs: 折纸风（Origami）是遵循法则的折痕和平面化的雕塑感。拼贴（Collage）是拼装起来的碎片。
纸艺风则是把撕裂的纸浆当作整个世界，一个剪影立在纤维之上。如果边缘是折叠的，你想要的是折纸风。
如果是粘贴的碎片，那是拼贴。
examples_film: 《辉夜姬物语》（The Tale of the Princess Kaguya）把纸和铅笔当作有生命的画面质感来处理。定格动画式的纸艺片头和剪纸短片，是最广为人知的应用。
纤维和撕裂是语法，而不是要照搬的某个片头。
mistakes: 一个人拿着纸当道具，或滑向了折纸风的折痕。破绽是没有撕裂，也没有纤维。
修正方法：剪影、纸浆的纹理，以及把撕裂的纸张质感当作整个世界。

faq.q: 电影中的纸艺风（Paper）是什么？
faq.a: 一种纸浆材质的风格：撕裂的质感、可见的纤维，一个人是一个剪影。整个世界就是那张纸，而不是手里的一件道具。

faq.q: 纸艺风（Paper）与折纸风（Origami）的区别
faq.a: 纸艺风是撕裂和纤维。折纸风是折痕和折面。如果这个世界是按照法则折叠的，你想要的是折纸风。
片头字幕、剪影世界、把纸浆当作场景。跳过整齐的折叠，以及拿书当道具的图书馆肖像。

faq.q: 如何为AI图像或视频撰写纸艺风的提示词？
faq.a: 先写掠射光，然后要求出现纤维和撕裂。禁止折纸风式的折痕。

narrative: Titles, stop-motion paper, a figure that has been scissored from stock: hard or window light that shows the edge of the sheet, fibers in the tear. Collage stacks pieces.
Paper is the material of the whole world. It is the wrong tool when the paper is neatly folded into facets, and the wrong tool when the person is simply standing in a library.
Show the cut and the fiber.
how: Eye height, 35mm to 50mm, lock-off. Light that rakes the tooth of the stock.
Torn edges, visible fibers, cut-out person. Prompt: Paper world of [Subject], torn stock, visible fibers, a person as a cut-out on pulp.
when: A title still, a cut-out figure, a world that is stock. Do not use it as origami, and do not use it as a person holding a sheet as a prop.
vs: Origami is lawful creases and planar sculpture. Collage is assembled pieces.
Paper is torn pulp as the world, a cut-out on fibers. If the edges are folded, you wanted origami.
If they are glued fragments, collage.
examples_film: The Tale of the Princess Kaguya treats paper and pencil as living stock. Stop-motion paper titles and cut-out shorts are the well-known use.
Fiber and tear as grammar, not a title to copy.
mistakes: A person holding paper as a prop, or a slide into Origami folds. The tell is no tear and no fiber.
Fix it: cut-out, pulp tooth, torn stock as the world.

faq.a: A pulp-material look: torn stock, visible fibers, a person as a cut-out. The world is the sheet, not a prop in a hand.
Paper is tear and fiber. Origami is crease and facet. If the world folds on lawful lines, you wanted origami.
Titles, cut-out worlds, pulp as set. Skip neat folds and library portraits with a book as a prop.

faq.q: How do I prompt Paper for AI image or video?
faq.a: Raking light, then: Paper world of [Subject], torn stock, visible fibers, a person as a cut-out on pulp. Demand fibers and a tear. Forbid origami creases.
